description: Cut a clip or several segments out of a video and (optionally) join them.

accurate.description: always re-encode for frame-accurate (video) / sample-accurate (audio) cuts (default: lossless -c copy, re-encoding only when the keyframe snap exceeds --tolerance)

argv.description: raw CLI arguments (non-canonical compatibility path; when present every other key is ignored)

codec.description: video encoder for the re-encode: h264 (x264, the default for SDR), hevc (x265, the default for HDR), av1 (SVT-AV1 or libaom), prores (422 HQ, needs a .mov/.mkv output); HDR sources keep their colour on hevc/av1/prores

declick_ms.description: --segments: fade the sound this many ms on each side of every join the re-encode makes, so butted cuts do not click (default 20; a stream-copy join is not faded)

dry_run.description: print the ffmpeg commands that would run, run nothing

edit_list.description: a single-segment .mp4/.mov stream copy keeps the MP4 edit list that hides the keyframe's pre-roll, so the picture starts at --start (the default since 3.0.0); a player that ignores edit lists shows the pre-roll

fast.description: preview quality: x264 preset veryfast (overrides --preset) for quick iterations

hw.description: encode on the GPU with Apple VideoToolbox (h264/hevc/prores; Apple Silicon only): several times faster, larger files at the same quality; falls back to the CPU encoder, reported, where it cannot apply

json_brief.description: like --json but trimmed: status, output, dry_run, verified, a compact summary of the output probe, this tool's own keys, and the command count instead of the command lines (failures print the full failure document, unchanged)

keep_hevc.description: a re-encode of an SDR HEVC source stays HEVC (x265 8-bit BT.709; VideoToolbox under --hw); the default since 3.0.0; --codec overrides it

min_confidence.description: refuse to snap below this measured beat confidence (default 0.5)

no_declick.description: --segments: butt the joins with no fade

no_edit_list.description: shift the copy's timestamps instead (-avoid_negative_ts make_zero, every 2.x release's default): the picture starts at the keyframe before --start

no_hw.description: encode on the CPU (x264/x265/SVT-AV1/prores_ks) even when $FFMPEG_SKILL_HW=1

no_keep_hevc.description: re-encode an SDR HEVC source with x264, as every 2.x release did (HDR still gets x265 Main10)

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output (refused without it)

plan.description: write the dry run as a plan (inputs fingerprinted, commands, expected output, verify steps) that render.py FILE executes later; implies --dry-run

quality.description: encoder quality on the CRF scale (default 18; lower = better; 18 visually lossless for x264/x265, up to 63 for av1); ignored by prores

remove.description: the inverse of --segments: drop these ranges and keep the rest, joined in order (e.g. '1:20-2:05,10:00-10:30'); overlapping ranges merge

segments.description: comma separated START-END list, e.g. '0:05-0:12,1:00-1:20' (joined in order)

smart.description: keyframe-aware cut of an H.264 source: re-encode only from each cut point to the next keyframe (and from the last keyframe to the end point), matched to the source's profile, level, pixel format, reorder depth and colour tags, and stream-copy the whole GOPs between; verified (frame grid, copied packets, decoded frames) or re-encoded in full with the reason in smart.reason

snap.description: move each in/out point to the nearest measured beat (default none)

snap_source.description: take the beat grid from this scenes.py --beats --json document (or from this media file) instead of measuring the input again

snap_tolerance.description: most seconds a point may move with --snap beats (default 0.12, about a quarter of a beat at 120 BPM)

start.description: start time (seconds, mm:ss or hh:mm:ss.ms). default 0

timeout.description: kill an ffmpeg run past this many seconds, kind=timeout (default 1800; 0 = no limit)

tolerance.description: max seconds a lossless cut may deviate before re-encoding kicks in (default 0.5, -1 = never for a keyframe snap; a --segments join is still re-cut for open GOPs, a later B-frame .mp4/.mov segment starting between keyframes, or a failed join check)

vfr_guard.description: what keeps a variable-frame-rate source from a stream copy (default sampled since 3.0.0: re-encode only when sampled packet timestamps are variable or too few to judge; average, every 2.x release's default: a nominal rate that differs from the average re-encodes, as --accurate, and the sampled timing is reported; off: measure and keep the copy, with a note)

name: cut
